prompt_basis: prompt_natural.md (natural prompt describing the helper-bypassing inline duplication in the TLV marshalling and accessory-clone modules)

rubrics.criterion: In src/tlv.c, the entry point that flattens nested TLV values into a stored flat record (tlv_add_tlv_value) performs record serialization and record appending again through the module's shared single-purpose steps (the module's formatting pass and its record-append routine, or consolidated equivalents) instead of carrying its own inline implementations of those steps.
rubrics.rationale: This site absorbed the serialization pass plus the append step; the natural prompt's core ask is that the flatten path delegate again, so grading must verify this specific path was actually re-delegated.

rubrics.criterion: In src/tlv.c, the entry point that parses a flat nested-TLV record back into values (tlv_get_tlv_value) performs lookup, destination-list construction and chunk-grouping parsing again through the module's shared steps (its parse routine and record-append routine, or consolidated equivalents) instead of its own inline implementations.
rubrics.rationale: The parse side absorbed the deepest local chain (lookup -> construct -> parse -> append); an equivalent sound refactoring may consolidate these steps, but leaving any self-contained inline parse at this entry point means the central ask was not met.

rubrics.criterion: In src/tlv.c, the entry point that writes a nested TLV tree into the flushing byte-stream sink (tlv_stream_add_tlv_value) delegates again to the module's shared step that writes a value into the sink (including its put/flush helpers or consolidated equivalents) rather than open-coding serialization plus guarded per-byte sink writes inline.
rubrics.rationale: This path absorbed the sink discipline (per-byte put with buffer-full flush) at every write site; the prompt calls out the stream write as one of the affected responsibilities, so this re-delegation must be verifiable on its own.

rubrics.criterion: In src/accessories.c, per-format value copying exists again as one shared implementation that the clone path invokes: homekit_value_clone delegates its copying to the module's value-copy routine (or a single consolidated equivalent), and homekit_characteristic_clone no longer carries its own independent dispatch-and-copy implementation of the same operation.
rubrics.rationale: The value-copy step exists in two divergent embedded copies (one at each clone site); the duplication of one representational step across two sites is the heart of this instance, so the rubric verifies one authoritative implementation is reused by both clone paths.

rubrics.criterion: The destination-offset alignment arithmetic used by homekit_characteristic_clone's packed layout (rounding up to sizeof(void*)) is expressed through one shared definition applied at the size-computation and pointer-advance sites (for example a restored helper equivalent to the module's alignment routine), instead of open-coded modulo/rounding formulas repeated inline at every packing offset.
rubrics.rationale: The inlining rework open-coded align-size formulas at every offset site and removed the module's pointer-alignment helper; the prompt explicitly asks for this arithmetic to live in one shared place again, making it an independently gradeable core outcome.

rubrics.criterion: No function in src/tlv.c or src/accessories.c retains an absorbed implementation: after the patch there is no monolith-profile function that contains a body-duplicate of a still-defined same-module routine it never calls (specifically none of the five maintained entry-point functions still embeds a re-implementation of the module's formatting pass, record append, chunk-grouping parse, sink put/flush, value copy, or alignment math).
rubrics.rationale: Guards the core failure mode of this instance: partially or cosmetically reworking one site while leaving the swallowed bodies in others (or moving a swallowed body into a new wrapper helper) still leaves the deep-inline relation in place.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is contained to internal structure of the two modules: code outside src/tlv.c and src/accessories.c (server, characteristics wiring, headers consumed elsewhere) requires no change for the tree to build and behave as before, and none of the shared steps' other consumers (for example the code paths that copy or marshal accessory values elsewhere) is broken by the re-delegation.
rubrics.rationale: The swallowed sub-methods are shared dependencies with callers outside the reworked entry points; a solver patch that forces ripple edits elsewhere, or that changes what external consumers of those shared steps observe, has not respected the dependency boundary of this task.

rubrics.criterion: The exported API of the two modules is frozen exactly: every exported function keeps its name, signature, return type, and value-ownership contract (in particular the five maintained entry points, the format/parse/stream/append/value-copy routines, and the accessory/characteristic/value clone functions; adding static-internal helpers is allowed, exporting new symbols or changing existing ones is not).
rubrics.rationale: The prompt fixes the compatibility boundary at unchanged public signatures and ownership contracts; this is the concrete associated obligation that keeps the repair auditable against this instance rather than an open redesign.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not leave formerly-absorbed shared routines defined yet unreachable: every shared step of the two modules (formatting pass, record append, chunk-grouping parse, sink value writer, value-copy routine, alignment helpers) is either genuinely back in use by the re-delegated paths or has been superseded by a consolidated equivalent (in which case the superseded definition is removed), so no live sub-method is left with only the inlined copies as its ghost callers.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible half-repair rewires some entry points but leaves one orphaned duplicate pair (helper still defined, callers all gone), which recreates the drift hazard this case is about; this rubric catches that residue.

rubrics.criterion: No dead code is left behind by the rework: every static function defined in src/tlv.c and src/accessories.c after the patch has an actual call site (no unused restored helper, no newly extracted helper that nothing calls).
rubrics.rationale: The cleanup obligation specific to this instance: the inline rework left/removed helpers (for example the deleted alignment helper whose formula was open-coded), and a repair that reintroduces or extracts helpers without wiring them leaves exactly the artifact residue the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The duplicated inline implementations are actually deleted from the code, not parked: no leftover commented-out blocks, '#if 0' regions, or unreachable duplicate fragments of the absorbed steps remain inside the two modules' functions.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific failure mode: 'removing' duplication by disabling or hiding the copies instead of deleting them would leave the module carrying ghost implementations that drift back into the maintenance hazard the task describes.

rubrics.criterion: Parsing of chunked nested records does not regress: continuation-record merging stays bound by the lookahead-derived total size (no copying a following record's payload as extra chunk data), a record declaring length zero still produces no value node and does not cause the scan to mis-advance or loop, and a missing record still yields no value.
rubrics.rationale: These are the exact parse semantics the flatten/parse paths must preserve on this instance (including some non-obvious original behaviors such as non-advancing zero-length records), and they are easy to break while reshaping chunk handling into shared steps.

rubrics.criterion: Stream-sink observable behavior is unchanged: the write callback still fires when the sink buffer fills then the position resets; serializing an empty nested value into the stream still emits the bare type/zero-length header pair; and the flatten path still serializes a zero-length item as a bare header pair followed by no payload bytes.
rubrics.rationale: The empty-value emission and the per-byte flush discipline are load-bearing observable behaviors of this instance's stream path; a repaired decomposition that routes these cases differently but with identical behavior passes, whereas dropping the header pair or skipping the callback breaks observed output formats.

rubrics.criterion: Value and characteristic cloning stay byte-faithful: cloned values preserve format tag, is_null/is_static flags, string duplication, raw data copy, and nested TLV duplication; the packed characteristic destination layout is unchanged, including reproducing the existing element-size accounting at the valid-values-range memcpy/pointer-advance site rather than normalizing the historical sizeof choice.
rubrics.rationale: The clone sites carry an idiosyncratic but deliberately preserved layout accounting (struct-size at the size site, pointer-size at the copy/advance site); 'fixing' it during the refactor would silently change replicated state layout relative to what this repository's tests and downstream persistence expect.

rubrics.criterion: Allocation-failure behavior of the reworked paths is preserved exactly: the TLV add path still fails with TLV_ERROR_MEMORY when its allocations fail; the parse path still releases the partially built value and returns NULL when an allocation fails; a record-node allocation failure in the parse path is still tolerated silently rather than propagated.
rubrics.rationale: These paths' memory-failure semantics (including the historically tolerated node-allocation failure) were deliberately carried through the maintenance change in this instance; altering which failure paths free or return what is a concrete case-specific regression.

rubrics.criterion: The re-delegation does not introduce repeated-copy or cleanup regressions in the previously absorbed error paths: no new double-free of record values, no leaking of the flat buffer on the early-error paths (relative to the module's documented original ownership behavior), and no stacked ownership change caused by calling a shared step that already manages its own memory.
rubrics.rationale: When a copy of inline logic is replaced by a call to a shared routine that allocates or owns data, ownership coupling is the instance-specific risk: the swallowed code and the shared step must not both manage the same memory.
